explanations.explanation: This neuron fires on tokens that kick off a new block or section—i.e. the very first word after a paragraph/segment boundary (whether it’s a Swedish “så” at the top of a news blurb, an all-caps “FILED” in a court header, a band name like FILUR, etc.). It’s essentially a “start-of-block” marker.

This neuron is essentially an “emphasis/evaluation” detector: it lights up on semantically rich content words—especially adjectives and adverbs—that carry strong descriptive or subjective weight (e.g. disastrous, lucrative, impressive, inherently, bizarre, ruthless, horrific, funny, etc.), signaling points of evaluative emphasis or stance in the text.

explanations.explanation: This feature picks up the uppercase “FIL” sequence as it appears in court‐document metadata—most often the “FILED” label (and its variants) that marks the filing date/number lines at the head of appellate opinions and dockets.
This feature is essentially a detector for the English definite article “the,” i.e. it lights up whenever the model is referencing a specific, previously identified entity or noun phrase.
